title: Aave V3 wstETH CAPO snapshot misalignment and E-Mode liquidations
summary: On 10 Mar 2026 at 11:46:11Z the newly launched Chaos Labs CAPO Risk Agent updated the wstETH price-cap adapter on Aave V3 Ethereum Core and Prime. The on-chain 3% step limit allowed the snapshotRatio to rise only from 1.1572 to 1.1919, but the snapshotTimestamp was set to 7 days earlier. The resulting cap (1.19395) sat below the live stETH-per-wstETH rate (1.22885), so Aave's wstETH price fell 2.84% with no market move. In the same block and the next six (84 s), 49 liquidations seized 10,938.6 wstETH (about $27M) from 35 E-Mode accounts with HF below about 1.029. wstETH borrow caps were cut to 1 at 13:56:59Z, and a Risk Steward realigned the snapshot at 15:53:59Z. No bad debt was incurred. The DAO approved a 512.19 ETH refund, net about 317 ETH after builder and searcher recoveries, distributed by about 1 Apr 2026.

positions_considered.description: Looper: wstETH collateral, WETH debt in ETH-correlated E-Mode on Aave V3 Core or Prime; health factor about 1.02 (aggressive) at the live exchange rate
wstETH collateral, USDC debt on Aave V3 Core (non-E-Mode); health factor about 1.5

t_incident_start.description: CAPO parameter update tx 0x32c64151 (block 24626860) caps the wstETH ratio 2.84% below the live rate.

t_first_public_signal.description: The on-chain CapParametersUpdated event and the price drop with ETH/USD flat are observable in the same block. The first text signal is @ltvprotocol at 12:50:28Z (+64 min). The precursor is Chaos Labs' 16 Feb forum post announcing CAPO automation with a 3% step limit, while the adapter's snapshot had been stale since Feb 2024.

t_point_of_no_return.definition: For wsteth_coll_weth_debt_emode with HF < 1.0288: the oracle had already mispriced the collateral and the liquidation landed in the same block (back-run). This archetype's PONR is the first wrong liquidation itself. wsteth_coll_usdc_debt at HF about 1.5 never reached a PONR: a 2.84% price cut lowers HF to about 1.46.

t_protocol_first_ack.description: On-chain wstETH borrow cap cut to 1 on Core and Prime (2 h 11 min after the update). The first written public acknowledgement is the Chaos Labs post-mortem at 19:50:36Z. LlamaRisk says it detected the anomaly within minutes, but flagged it privately.

lead_time_minutes.notes: The lead time is zero. The first wrong liquidation was in the same block as the oracle update (block 24626860), and 93% of the volume (10,130.6 of 10,938.6 wstETH) was liquidated within 12 s. Measured from the first text signal (@ltvprotocol 12:50:28Z) the lead time is -64 min, and from the first written protocol acknowledgement (19:50:36Z) it is -484 min. Only a pre-incident signal could have helped, namely the visibly stale snapshot plus the announced Risk Agent launch. That is a structural reason to keep loopers at a higher HF, not a timed alert.

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: At HF about 1.02 (below 1.0288), liquidated in the first seconds. The loss was the 2.84% price gap on the liquidated collateral plus the liquidation bonus. Across all users the oracle loss was 382.76 ETH and the bonus 129.72 ETH. The DAO refunded in ETH, distributed by about 1 Apr 2026. One user reported being about 20 WETH short. A looper at HF of 1.03 or above was not liquidated.
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: About 4-5% of liquidated collateral value before refund, about 0 after refund (if the refund was complete)

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Not affected. A 2.84% lower collateral price for about 4 h moves HF from 1.5 to about 1.46. No liquidation, and withdrawals and repayments stayed open.

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: The market price did not move: ETH/USD was flat at about $2,062 and the stETH exchange rate unchanged. A market-price HF or LTV trigger would not fire. A trigger on Aave-reported HF would see the drop in the same block as the liquidations, which is too late. A rule keeping a buffer of at least 3% HF above 1.0 in E-Mode (HF of 1.03 or more) would have avoided the liquidation entirely, by structure rather than by timing.

ideal_action.rationale: Only a standing buffer helps. The announced CAPO automation (16 Feb) plus a snapshot stale since 2024 argued for holding HF of 1.05 or more. After 11:46:11Z, survivors near HF 1.0 at the capped price should reduce until the fix at 15:53:59Z.
A 2.84% oracle haircut does not threaten HF 1.5. Repay and withdraw stayed available.

expected_judge_labels.rationale: Nothing observable in the window; at most a structural note about the stale CAPO snapshot.
Collateral oracle 2.84% below the exchange rate; mass E-Mode liquidations. Raise HF until the cap is fixed.
Oracle restored. Remediation underway. Residual Risk Agent process risk.
Oracle haircut of 2.84%, but HF 1.5 has ample buffer.

data_gaps: No Aave, Chaos Labs, LlamaRisk or security-firm X post earlier than 12:50Z was found. LlamaRisk's 'within minutes' detection was private. Accounts such as @aave, @chaos_labs and @LlamaRisk may have posted earlier statuses we did not find.
The @yieldsandmore status 2031468808012210538 (2026-03-10T20:34:41Z), cited by rekt, returned no syndication text and is excluded.
Reimbursement distribution was not verified on-chain. Its timing (by about 26 Mar-1 Apr) comes from forum posts.
We count 35 liquidated addresses on-chain; Aave reports 34.
rekt.news body text was not parsed.
The DeFiLlama entry's add time is unknown.
source_quality: Primary on-chain data covers the CAPO events, adapter price and isCapped at about 15-30 min cadence, LiquidationCall logs on both pools, and BorrowCapChanged events. Block times are from Ethereum RPC (drpc/mevblocker). They match the post-mortem's 10,938 wstETH and about 2.85%. Forum times are Discourse created_at. X times are decoded from snowflake IDs, with text from syndication (some long posts truncated). News times come from article metadata; The Block was read through WebFetch because of a 403.

items.verbatim_text: This document presents a formal framework for dynamically calibrating the core parameters of the Correlated Asset Price Oracle (CAPO) system, namely maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent and snapshotRatio , through autonomous Risk Oracles. items.author: ChaosLabs
items.verbatim_text: A technical incident affecting the CAPO risk oracle caused the reported wstETH/stETH exchange rate cap to fall below the currently valid market exchange rate on Ethereum Core and Prime instances. This resulted in an approximately 2.85% decrease in the effective exchange rate used by the protocol, triggering roughly 10938 wstETH in E-Mode liquidations. During this, protocol incurred no bad debt. However, liquidators captured approximately 512 ETH in liquidation bonuses and value realized through the exchange rate deviation.

items.author: LlamaRisk
items.verbatim_text: On March 10, 2026, a newly deployed CAPO Risk Agent pushed a parameter update that artificially depressed the wstETH oracle price by approximately 2.85%, triggering roughly $26.6 million in liquidation volume across Aave V3 Core and Prime markets. LlamaRisk detected the anomalous liquidation activity within minutes and immediately flagged the issue to other service providers. ... We can observe what lands onchain, but we cannot audit what generates it.
